The **Air raid on Ceylon (5 April 1942)** also known as the **Easter Sunday raid**, was an air attack on [Colombo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombo "Colombo"), [British Ceylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Ceylon "British Ceylon") (now Sri Lanka) by [Imperial Japanese Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Japanese_Navy "Imperial Japanese Navy") aircraft from the [aircraft carriers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier "Aircraft carrier") of the [1st Air Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Air_Fleet "1st Air Fleet") (_Kidō Butai_) during the Indian Ocean raid (31 March – 10 April 1942). The Japanese plan was to destroy the British [Eastern Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Fleet "Eastern Fleet") in harbour.

The British received warning of the raid in March through decoded Japanese wireless messages and from [air reconnaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_reconnaissance "Air reconnaissance"). The British forestalled the Japanese by dispersing shipping from the harbours in Ceylon before the attack. The Japanese aircraft were met by fighters of [222 Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._222_Group_RAF "No. 222 Group RAF"), [Royal Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Air_Force "Royal Air Force"), the [Fleet Air Arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_Air_Arm "Fleet Air Arm") (FAA) of the [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy") and [anti-aircraft guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_guns "Anti-aircraft guns").

Port facilities were damaged and ships in Colombo harbour were sunk or damaged. The bulk of the Eastern Fleet was not found and survived but several ships were sunk at sea after the raid. The Eastern Fleet moved temporarily to [East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa "East Africa"), from where it sent carrier forces into the central and eastern Indian Ocean. The Japanese Navy was unable to repeat the raid because of its commitments in the Pacific.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

### British Ceylon (Sri Lanka)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: British Ceylon (Sri Lanka)")]

Main article: [British Ceylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Ceylon "British Ceylon")

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Colombo_Map_1930.jpg/250px-Colombo_Map_1930.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colombo_Map_1930.jpg)

1930 diagram of Colombo and the harbour

Ceylon (now [Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka "Sri Lanka")) is off the south-east of India between shipping routes from [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore") and [Rangoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangoon "Rangoon") to the [Red Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea "Red Sea") and the [Persian Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf"). There are natural harbours at Colombo on the south-western coast and Trincomalee on the north-eastern coast, a naval anchorage and base.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014384-2) Ceylon was a geographically important part of the British Empire and its system of trade, communication and military organisation. In the 1930s more shipping tonnage was handled in Ceylon than all the ports of India. Since the beginning of the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), the colonial government had engaged in mass recruitment for local defence, overseas labouring and expanded food production.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJackson2006308-3) Tea and rubber production was emphasised and rubber output rose from 99,500 long tons (101,100 t) in 1941 to 105,500 long tons (107,200 t) in 1943.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurstfield1953168-4) The 3,600 workers in civil engineering converted to the repair and refitting of ships and the manufacture of dummy aircraft, guns and radar installations.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJackson2006308-3)

When the [Pacific War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_War "Pacific War") began on 7 December 1941, the Allied disasters in the Pacific, Malaya and the British débâcle at the [Battle of Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Singapore "Battle of Singapore") in February 1942 made [Colombo Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombo_Harbour "Colombo Harbour") the basis for eastern trade and the centre for the assembly of Indian Ocean convoys. Colombo port was large enough for 45 ships but soon had 100 to 110 ships at once, causing much overcrowding.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMOD1995122-5) The strategic importance of Ceylon increased and British planners deemed the island essential to the defence of [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") and Allied lines of communication through the Indian Ocean. The Allied defeat in the [Dutch East Indies campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_East_Indies_campaign "Dutch East Indies campaign") (11 January – 9 March 1942) left the Indian Ocean vulnerable to Japanese attacks.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBoyd2017364%E2%80%93359-6) The [Malacca Strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malacca_Strait "Malacca Strait") in the Netherlands East Indies was about 1,000 nmi (1,900 km; 1,200 mi) east of Trincomalee, making it a useful base for attacks on Japanese ships sailing to Rangoon in Burma.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014384-2)

From September to December 1941, 710 troop reinforcements arrived on the island and from January to March 1942, another 2,612 arrived; during April and June, 2,112 more troops joined the garrison (2,872) and 4,993 troops moved between the Far East and Ceylon from October 1941 to March 1942.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBehrens1955245,_278-7) The extent of the disasters that befell the British in early 1942, led in March to Admiral Sir [Geoffrey Layton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Layton "Geoffrey Layton") being transferred from the temporary command of the [Eastern Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Fleet "Eastern Fleet") and installed as the Commander-in-Chief, Ceylon, after Admiral [James Somerville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Somerville "James Somerville") arrived to command the fleet. Layton was given authority over the military forces on the island and the civilian authorities of the governor, Sir [Andrew Caldecott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Caldecott "Andrew Caldecott"), "Do not ask permission to do things. Do them and report afterwards what you have done".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJackson2006314,_310-8) Layton found the same complacency and inertia in Ceylon as he had experienced in Malaya,

> ...he takes complete charge of Ceylon and stands no nonsense from anyone.... He pulls all the Ministers legs... and they work for him all the harder.

—Admiral Somerville[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoskill195623%E2%88%9224-9)

### Air defence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Air defence")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Fairey_Fulmar_Mk_I_%28M4062%29.jpg/250px-Fairey_Fulmar_Mk_I_%28M4062%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fairey_Fulmar_Mk_I_(M4062).jpg)

Example of a Fairey Fulmar Mk II

In September 1941 the [Royal Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Air_Force "Royal Air Force") (RAF) had established [No. 222 Group RAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._222_Group_RAF "No. 222 Group RAF") (Air Vice-Marshal [John D'Albiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_D'Albiac "John D'Albiac")) on the island in command of [273 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._273_Squadron_RAF "No. 273 Squadron RAF") at [China Bay airfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Bay_Airport "China Bay Airport") with four [Vickers Vildebeest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vickers_Vildebeest "Vickers Vildebeest") and four [Fairey Seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairey_Seal "Fairey Seal")[torpedo bombers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torpedo_bomber "Torpedo bomber").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJackson2006314,_310-8) Until February 1942, the air defence of Ceylon had been a Royal Navy responsibility and [803 Naval Air Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/803_Naval_Air_Squadron "803 Naval Air Squadron") (803 NAS) and [806 Naval Air Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/806_Naval_Air_Squadron "806 Naval Air Squadron") (806 NAS) had transferred to Ceylon from the Middle East, six [Fairey Fulmars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairey_Fulmar "Fairey Fulmar") at a time. Eight Hurricanes that had been assembled at Karachi, were flown to Ceylon, six of the Hurricanes, ferried to Ceylon by pilots of [136 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._136_Squadron_RAF "No. 136 Squadron RAF"), arrived at [RAF Ratmalana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAF_Ratmalana "RAF Ratmalana") on 23 February. The Torpedo Bomber Reconnaissance Pool, [788 Naval Air Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/788_Naval_Air_Squadron "788 Naval Air Squadron") (788 NAS) with six [Fairey Swordfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairey_Swordfish "Fairey Swordfish") for the Eastern Fleet, was formed on 18 January at China Bay, near [Trincomalee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trincomalee "Trincomalee") and was pressed into service in defence of Ceylon.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWragg2001136ShoresCullIzawa2014384-10)

By March 1942, there were airfields at China Bay near Trincomalee, Ratmalana near Colombo, an airstrip was built at the [Colombo Racecourse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombo_Racecourse "Colombo Racecourse") to relieve congestion at Ratmalana and another airstrip had been built at [Minneriya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minneriya "Minneriya") on the south coast. China Bay was a grass landing ground that had the sea at both ends and there was a ridge along the southern edge; a low ridge ran along the northern boundary. Aircraft could only land and take off to the north-east or south-west, depending on the wind direction. There were fuel storage tanks beyond the north-east corner of the airfield at the Royal Naval Base Trincomalee.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014384-2) Anti-aircraft defence comprised four obsolescent [QF 3-inch 20 cwt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QF_3-inch_20_cwt "QF 3-inch 20 cwt")[anti-aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft "Anti-aircraft") guns at Trincomalee. The danger of an air attack by aircraft of the Japanese Navy aircraft carriers was acute after the examples of the [Attack on Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor "Attack on Pearl Harbor") in December 1941 and the [Bombing of Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombing_of_Darwin "Bombing of Darwin") in February 1942.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201433-1) The airfields at Ratmalana, near Colombo and China Bay had been expanded.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTERichardsSaunders197570-11)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-13)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/RIHB_2022_PBY_Catalina.jpg/250px-RIHB_2022_PBY_Catalina.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RIHB_2022_PBY_Catalina.jpg)

Example of a Catalina flying boat

On 6 and 7 March the aircraft carrier [HMS _Indomitable_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Indomitable_(92) "HMS Indomitable (92)") dispatched sixty Hurricanes of [30 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._30_Squadron_RAF "No. 30 Squadron RAF") and [261 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._261_Squadron_RAF "No. 261 Squadron RAF"), that had been intended for Java. On 30 March, the RAF reconstituted [258 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._258_Squadron_RAF "No. 258 Squadron RAF") that had been mauled in the fighting in [British Malaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Malaya "British Malaya"), [Sumatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumatra "Sumatra") and [Java](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java "Java").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJackson2006314-14) By 4 April, 803 NAS and 806 NAS of the [Fleet Air Arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_Air_Arm "Fleet Air Arm") were ready with 24 Fulmars; the ground defences had been reinforced to 144 anti-aircraft guns. On 5 April, there were 37–38 serviceable Hurricanes near Colombo.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201444,_42,_35-15)

The first [Consolidated PBY Catalina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consolidated_PBY_Catalina "Consolidated PBY Catalina") long-range flying boat of [413 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/413_Squadron "413 Squadron")[Royal Canadian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Canadian_Air_Force "Royal Canadian Air Force") (RCAF) arrived on 28 March, with the ground crews following on by sea, two more arrived before the raid and on 6 and 7 April two more Canadian Catalinas arrived.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGreenhous1994386-16) By 4 April, four [205 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._205_Squadron_RAF "No. 205 Squadron RAF") RAF Catalinas had reached the island. There was one operational Dutch Catalina of the [Netherlands Naval Aviation Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_Naval_Aviation_Service "Netherlands Naval Aviation Service") (MLD); two of the RAF and three Dutch Catalinas were unserviceable. The Catalinas were based at [Koggala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koggala_Airport "Koggala Airport")[lagoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koggala_Lagoon "Koggala Lagoon"), at the south end of the island.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201433,_35,_44,_37-12)

### Radar

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Radar")]

Main article: [Air Ministry Experimental Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Ministry_Experimental_Station "Air Ministry Experimental Station")

Radar stations, code-named Air Ministry Experimental Stations (AMES) were established at the [Royal Colombo Golf Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Colombo_Golf_Club "Royal Colombo Golf Club") at Ridgeway about 6 mi (9.7 km) north of Ratmalana airfield (AMES 254) and at Trincomalee (AMES 272). AMES 254 personnel arrived on 18 March and the equipment four days later. AMES 254 became operational on 25 March and was linked by telephone to 20 Operations Room on 28 March. The terrain around the radar limited maximum range to 60 mi (97 km) and the altitude of an object affected the detection range. The short notice may not have been sufficient for operators to tell the difference between false radar echoes produced by local conditions and real ones. The aerial projected "[lobes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiation_pattern "Radiation pattern")" in which objects might be detected, with gaps between some lobes or lobes overlapping. The distance travelled by an aircraft between the maximum range of AMES 254 to Ratmalana was 54 mi (87 km) A Zero took about 17 minutes to cover the distance and it took a Hurricane five minutes to take off and six more to climb to interception altitude. There were only six minutes for AMES 254 to report to 20 Operations Room and for orders to be issued if pilots were going to avoid being caught climbing.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201439%E2%80%9341-17)

### Japanese preparations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Japanese preparations")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/Pacific_War_-_Southern_Asia_1942_-_Map.jpg/250px-Pacific_War_-_Southern_Asia_1942_-_Map.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pacific_War_-_Southern_Asia_1942_-_Map.jpg)

The [Indian Ocean raid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean_raid "Indian Ocean raid") of the Japanese [Combined Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combined_Fleet "Combined Fleet") (31 March to 10 April 1942)

On 9 March 1942 the Japanese [Combined Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combined_Fleet "Combined Fleet") (Admiral [Chūichi Nagumo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C5%ABichi_Nagumo "Chūichi Nagumo")) was ordered to protect Japanese sea communications from attack by the British army in Burma and to "sweep the Bay of Bengal clear of British naval units", ready for the occupation of the [Andaman Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andaman_Islands "Andaman Islands") and the [Nicobar Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicobar_Islands "Nicobar Islands") in the eastern Indian Ocean. In February 1942, the Japanese army and navy conducted a war game to examine an invasion of Ceylon but both services were lukewarm. The army did not have the troops for an invasion and occupation; the navy was preoccupied with its operations in the Pacific.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBoyd2017366%E2%80%93367,_373MOD1995247-18)

There were insufficient ships to shift an invasion force and supply a garrison against attacks by British ships, submarines and aircraft. The Prime Minister, [Hideki Tojo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hideki_Tojo "Hideki Tojo"), rejected the plan indefinitely.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStille202330-19) By 16 March, the plan for an [Indian Ocean raid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean_raid "Indian Ocean raid") was to depart from [Staring Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staring_Bay "Staring Bay") in the [Celebes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebes "Celebes") (now [Sulawesi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulawesi "Sulawesi")) in the [Netherlands East Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_East_Indies "Netherlands East Indies") on 26 March, ready to attack Colombo on 5 April (C day). The Combined Fleet was based on the five aircraft carriers of the 1st Air Fleet, comprising [_Akagi_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_aircraft_carrier_Akagi "Japanese aircraft carrier Akagi") of the 1st Carrier Squadron, [_Sōryū_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_aircraft_carrier_S%C5%8Dry%C5%AB "Japanese aircraft carrier Sōryū") and [_Hiryū_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_aircraft_carrier_Hiry%C5%AB "Japanese aircraft carrier Hiryū") of the 2nd Carrier Squadron, with [_Shōkaku_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_aircraft_carrier_Sh%C5%8Dkaku "Japanese aircraft carrier Shōkaku") and [_Zuikaku_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_aircraft_carrier_Zuikaku "Japanese aircraft carrier Zuikaku") of the 5th Carrier Squadron.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBoyd2017366%E2%80%93367,_373MOD1995247-18)

### British code-breaking

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: British code-breaking")]

On 4 December 1941 the Japanese had altered their code [JN-25B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_naval_codes#JN-25 "Japanese naval codes") that prevented British code-breakers of the [Far East Combined Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far_East_Combined_Bureau "Far East Combined Bureau") (FECB) since 1936, a station of the [Government Code and Cypher School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_Code_and_Cypher_School "Government Code and Cypher School") (GC&CS) at [Bletchley Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bletchley_Park "Bletchley Park") in England.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStephenson202292-20) from reading Japanese wireless messages. On 3 March 1942, the British began reading JN-25B messages again. By the middle of the month, decrypts revealed that the 1st Carrier Squadron and the 2nd Carrier Squadron were at Staring Bay in the Celebes, an [Imperial Japanese Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Japanese_Navy "Imperial Japanese Navy") fuelling base and that the 5th Carrier Squadron was en route. Around 20 March decrypts revealed that a carrier force in Area D was going to attack DG on 2 April (C Day). On 28 March it was inferred that DG was Colombo. Japanese preparations were delayed by the late arrival of the 5th Carrier Squadron at Staring Bay on 24 March and the fleet sailed on 26 March.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBoyd2017366%E2%80%93370-21)

The British air defences in Ceylon were alerted for an attack on 1 or 2 March and merchant shipping dispersed from Colombo. The Eastern Fleet sortied on 30 March to patrol 100 mi (160 km) south of the island. Aerial reconnaissance by Catalina flying-boats concentrated on the south-east, the right direction that the Japanese would approach but with no sightings, the Eastern Fleet retired late on 2 April toward [Addu Atoll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addu_Atoll "Addu Atoll") to refuel at [Gan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gan_(Addu_Atoll) "Gan (Addu Atoll)") (Port T) about 600 mi (970 km) south-west of Ceylon. The heavy cruisers [HMS _Cornwall_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Cornwall_(56) "HMS Cornwall (56)") and [_Dorsetshire_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Dorsetshire_(40) "HMS Dorsetshire (40)") sailed for [Colombo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombo "Colombo") and [HMS _Hermes_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Hermes_(95) "HMS Hermes (95)") set out for Trincomalee to resume their commitments.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBoyd2017366%E2%80%93370-21)

## Prelude

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Prelude")]

### 2−4 April

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2−4 April")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/HEkXrqUaAAE3cZM.jpg/250px-HEkXrqUaAAE3cZM.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HEkXrqUaAAE3cZM.jpg)

The deck of the Japanese aircraft carrier _Akagi_ before the Indian Ocean raid

During the morning of 2 April, three [Kawanishi H6K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawanishi_H6K "Kawanishi H6K") flying boats from [Port Blair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Blair "Port Blair") made a reconnaissance flight towards Ceylon and early on 4 April, an H6K was sent to Trincomalee, observing eight merchant ships and a destroyer in the harbour.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014394-22) The Japanese cancelled a planned reconnaissance of Colombo harbour on 4 April by cruiser floatplanes.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBoyd2017369-23) Before dawn on 4 April, Catalina QL-A of 413 Squadron RCAF, flown by Squadron Leader [Leonard Birchall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Birchall "Leonard Birchall"), took off from Koggala to reconnoitre the southern-most patrol sector.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBoyd2017368-24)

Later in the day, the crew decided to repeat a leg that took them to the southern-most point of their patrol. At 16:00, the crew spotted the Japanese fleet on the southern horizon, about 360 nmi (670 km; 410 mi) south-east of Ceylon.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBoyd2017368-24) Three Zeros from _Akagi_, three from _Zuikaku_ and six from _Hiryū_ attacked the Catalina as it closed to get an accurate sighting. The radio was destroyed mid-transmission and only the sighting not the size of the fleet was received at Ceylon; several minutes after the Zeros attack began, QL-A was forced down on the sea.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201468%E2%80%9369,_37Boyd2017368-25)

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Leonard_birchall.jpg/250px-Leonard_birchall.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Leonard_birchall.jpg)

Squadron Leader [Leonard Birchall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Birchall "Leonard Birchall") RCAF, pilot of the Catalina that spotted the Japanese fleet

Zeroes [strafed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strafe "Strafe") and sank the Catalina, the front gunner had been killed and two of the crew were shot in the water. The six survivors, including Birchall, were captured by the Japanese destroyer[_Isokaze_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_destroyer_Isokaze_(1939) "Japanese destroyer Isokaze (1939)"). The prisoners claimed to have taken off from Colombo and this was reported to the fleet flagship _Akagi_ late in the day; Koggala was not attacked during the raid. The prisoners denied making a sighting report but were confounded when the Japanese intercepted a signal from Colombo asking QL-A to repeat its report.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201436-26)

Catalina FV-R from 205 Squadron, flown by [Flight Lieutenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_Lieutenant "Flight Lieutenant") "Jock" Graham, took off at 17:45. FV-R made reports at 22:37 of a destroyer at [01°59′N 82°20′E / 1.983°N 82.333°E / 1.983; 82.333](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&params=01_59_N_82_20_E_), course 315 degrees, speed 20 kn (37 km/h; 23 mph) and on 5 April at 00:45 reported six destroyers at [02°54′N 82°10′E / 2.900°N 82.167°E / 2.900; 82.167](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&params=02_54_N_82_10_E_), course 325 degrees, speed 21 kn (39 km/h; 24 mph) and at 06:15 a battleship, a cruiser "and at least four other ships" (Stuart 2014) 110 nmi (200 km; 130 mi), on a bearing of 195 degrees from [Dondra Head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dondra_Head "Dondra Head"), the southern tip of Ceylon. The Catalina was shot down by Japanese fighters about an hour and a half after making the report, with the loss of the crew.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201437-27)

## Attack on Colombo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Attack on Colombo")]

### 5 April

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 5 April")]

After the report from QL-A, D'Albiac briefed his staff for a Japanese air attack around dawn; 222 Group issued Operation Order No. 43 before midnight on 4 April,

> Should the enemy force maintain present reported course at a speed of 25 knots it will arrive in position approximately 150 miles from Colombo at 2100 hours G.M.T. [Greenwich Mean Time].[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201438-28)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Hawker_Sea_Hurricane_Mk.1b_%28Z7015%29_arrives_Fairford_7Jul2016_arp.jpg/250px-Hawker_Sea_Hurricane_Mk.1b_%28Z7015%29_arrives_Fairford_7Jul2016_arp.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hawker_Sea_Hurricane_Mk.1b_(Z7015)_arrives_Fairford_7Jul2016_arp.jpg)

Example of a Sea Hurricane Mk.1b

At 04:00 on 5 April the RAF and FAA squadrons were put on stand-by with pilots at _immediate readiness_; 803 NAS scrambled six Fulmars from Ratmalana to patrol from [Bentota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bentota "Bentota"), 35 mi (56 km) south of Colombo on the west coast, to [Pottuvri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pottuvil "Pottuvil")135 nmi (250 km; 155 mi) away on the south-east coast. The Navy ordered ships at Colombo and Trincomalee to scatter but at Colombo 21 merchant ships and 13 naval vessels were unable to sail due to defects and other reasons.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBoyd2017368ShoresCullIzawa2014394Stuart201437%E2%80%9339-29)_Cornwall_ and _Dorsetshire_ had departed from Colombo late on 4 April to rejoin the Eastern Fleet, part of which had started sailing back to Ceylon from Port T after the QL-A report.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoskill195627Boyd2017370-30)

At 05:34, Catalina BN-L of [240 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._240_Squadron_RAF "No. 240 Squadron RAF"), piloted by Flight Lieutenant W. Bradshaw, took off. At about 06:40, The crew saw six aircraft that looked like Fulmars at 5,000 ft (1,500 m) flying north in [vic formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vic_formation "Vic formation") through scattered cloud, about 100 nmi (190 km; 120 mi) south of Ceylon. Four more aircraft, also flying north, were taken to be [Sea Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawker_Hurricane_variants#Sea_Hurricanes "Hawker Hurricane variants"). Since the aircraft were "British", Bradshaw kept radio silence. A Japanese aircraft had spotted BN-L at 06:38 and signalled soon afterwards "Sighted enemy plane. One flying boat at 346 degrees, 43 nmi [80 km (50 mi)] from launch point.(Stuart 2014)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201438-28)

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Zero_Akagi_Dec1941.jpg/250px-Zero_Akagi_Dec1941.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zero_Akagi_Dec1941.jpg)

A [Mitsubishi A6M Zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitsubishi_A6M_Zero "Mitsubishi A6M Zero") fighter taking off.

At 06:00 53 Kate bombers began to take off, 18 from _Sōryū_, 18 from _Hiryū_ and 17 from _Akagi_, 120 nmi (220 km; 140 mi) from Colombo. Vals began to take off, 19 from _Shōkaku_ and 19 from _Zuikaku_ with 36 Zero fighter escorts forming a second wave.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014395-31) The Japanese aircraft approached Colombo from seaward, out of view of coast watchers and the 803 NAS line patrol. AMES 254 and its radar also failed to detect the Japanese force. British fighter pilots waited for a [scramble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scrambling_(military) "Scrambling (military)") that, due to the lack of early warning, never came, instead they were forced to take off during the attack, a tactical disadvantage when they needed height for the dive-and zoom tactic that could defeat the more manoeuvrable Zeros.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201435%E2%80%9344-32)

The first sign of a raid came at 07:32, when nine Zero fighters from _Hiryū_ flew over the Colombo Racecourse airfield. The Zeros from _Hiryū_ met six Swordfish of 788 NAS over Colombo, en route to Ratmalana, whose crews thought that the fighters were Hurricanes and fired the recognition signal (two greens). One pilot reported being attacked by "a Hurricane with a large red dot painted on the wings and fuselage"; the Six Swordfish were quickly shot down, the Zero pilots claiming eight aircraft. Five Hurricane Mk Ibs and nine Mk IIbs of 258 Squadron got off the ground undisturbed by 07:35 and climbed after the Zeros heading for the harbour. Three Fulmars each from 803 NAS and 806 NAS were scrambled from Ratmalana and the Racecourse. The 38 Vals from _Shōkaku_ and _Zuikaku_ were spotted from Ratmalana. The 14 Vals from _Zuikaku_ attacked the airfield at 07:45 as Hurricanes from 30 Squadron were taking off in ones and twos; 21 got off the ground but four had not when the first bombs fell. The commanding officer's Hurricane was damaged and crashed on take-off. Pilots with no aircraft to fly armed themselves with [Thompson submachine guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thompson_submachine_gun "Thompson submachine gun") and joined in with the airfield Bofors gunners.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014395%E2%80%93397_399-33)

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/Mk1_Hawker_Hurricane.jpg/250px-Mk1_Hawker_Hurricane.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mk1_Hawker_Hurricane.jpg)

RAF [Hawker Hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawker_Hurricane "Hawker Hurricane") Mk I

A few minutes after the attack by Vals from _Zuikaku_, Zeros from _Sōryū_ and _Akagi_ arrived and at 07:50 the Vals from _Shōkaku_ attacked. The three Fulmars of 803 NAS were shot down as they climbed away from the airfield and the 30 Squadron Hurricanes that got into the air were also bounced. At the harbour, 258 Squadron arrived as Vals began to dive. The Hurricanes attacked the Vals, later being credited with shooting down three and damaging several more but lost nine Hurricanes to the Japanese fighter escorts. Two of the remaining five Hurricanes were damaged and four pilots were killed.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014395%E2%80%93397_399-33) As the Hurricanes engaged the Vals and Zeros, Kates arrived from _Sōryū_ at 07:56, _Hiryū_ at 08:05 and _Akagi_ at 08:08 with fighter escorts from _Zuikaku_. Five Kates were damaged in the first two waves but the third wave and its escorts were unopposed and were on the way back by 08:15. The Vals from _Shōkaku_ took three minutes to bomb.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014402-34)

The Japanese bombers hit and set on fire the [armed merchant cruiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_merchant_cruiser "Armed merchant cruiser")[HMS _Hector_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Hector_(F45) "HMS Hector (F45)") with five bombs, settling it on the bottom. The [submarine depot ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine_depot_ship "Submarine depot ship")[HMS _Lucia_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Lucia "HMS Lucia") was damaged. Five Vals from _Zuikaku_ hit the British tanker [MV _San Cirilo_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_San_Cirilo?action=edit&redlink=1 "MV San Cirilo (page does not exist)") (8,012 GRT) and 53 Kates, sank the destroyer [HMS _Tenedos_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Tenedos_(H04) "HMS Tenedos (H04)"), killing 33 members of the crew.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrown199560-35) The bombers hit port facilities and damaged the merchant ship [SS _Benledi_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Empire_Admiral "SS Empire Admiral") (5,943 GRT), the Norwegian tanker [MV _Soli_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Soli?action=edit&redlink=1 "MV Soli (page does not exist)") (5,834 GRT) was damaged and beached; the British freighter [SS _Clan Murdoch_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Clan_Murdoch?action=edit&redlink=1 "SS Clan Murdoch (page does not exist)") (5,960 GRT) was damaged.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201442%E2%80%9343,_47Jordan2006127,_314,_564,_191,_116-36) The Zeros and the last Vals from _Zuikaku_ turned for home between 09:20 and 09:35. A flight of Fulmars from 803 NAS returned from a patrol, the crews unaware of the Japanese raid. The Japanese aircraft landed on their carriers from 09:45 to 10:30 and claimed a destroyer, a merchant ship and ten smaller vessels sunk; damage to Ratmalana airfield was negligible.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014402,_405-37)

### Subsequent events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Subsequent events")]

#### 11 Squadron

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 11 Squadron")]

Ten Blenheims of 11 Squadron took off at 08:30 to attack the Combined Fleet but were briefed with the wrong directions and failed to find the Japanese ships.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014405-38)

#### Reconnaissance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Reconnaissance")]

Catalinas based in Ceylon and Albacores from the Eastern Fleet continued to fly reconnaissance sorties during the day. At 08:40, three Zeros apiece from _Hiryū_, _Shōkaku_ and _Zuikaku_ shot down Catalina FV-R of 205 Squadron and killed the crew but not before the gunners damaged two of the Zeros from _Zuikaku_. Later on, three Zeros from _Hiryū_ attacked two 827 NAS Albacores from the Eastern Fleet and shot one down, the crew being killed. Another 827 NAS Albacore was attacked by Zeros from _Hiryū_ but escaped in cloud.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014405-38)

#### Sinking of _Dorsetshire_ and _Cornwall_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Sinking of Dorsetshire and Cornwall")]

Main article: [Loss of Dorsetshire and Cornwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean_raid#Loss_of_Dorsetshire_and_Cornwall "Indian Ocean raid")

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/E7k-8.jpg/250px-E7k-8.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:E7k-8.jpg)

[Kawanishi E7K2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawanishi_E7K2 "Kawanishi E7K2") (Alf) seaplane

Aircraft from Japanese cruisers searched the area south of Ceylon for the British ships that had not been found in port. At 10:50, a [Kawanishi E7K2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawanishi_E7K2 "Kawanishi E7K2") (Alf) from the Japanese cruiser [_Abukuma_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_cruiser_Abukuma "Japanese cruiser Abukuma"), found _Cornwall_ and _Dorsetshire_ but the crew reported that they had spotted two destroyers 200 nmi (370 km; 230 mi) west of the Striking Force, to the south-east of the Combined Fleet. _Cornwall_ was heading for Colombo to resume its refit and _Dorsetshire_ to escort a troop convoy.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStephenson2022252-39) The 5th Carrier Squadron, in reserve, with its aircraft loaded with bombs for another attack on Colombo, was ordered to attack the British cruisers instead.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014406Boyd2017372-40)

Rearming with torpedoes took too long and the 2nd Carrier Squadron attacked with 18 Vals from _Sōryū_, 18 from _Hiryū_ and 17 from _Akagi_. Thirty-seven aircraft carried 250 kg (551 lb) semi-armour piercing bombs and the other 16 were armed with 241 kg (532 lb) high-explosive bombs. The Vals from _Sōryū_ attacked out of the sun from 14:40 to 14:55 and claimed 14 hits. The Vals from _Hiryū_ commenced their attack soon after those from _Sōryū_ and the Vals from _Akagi_ claimed seven hits on one cruiser and eight hits on the other. _Dorsetshire_ was hit on its aircraft catapult, bridge, engine rooms and boiler rooms; the rudder jammed and the cruiser sank at 14:48. _Cornwall_ was hit by 15 bombs and sank six minutes later. The 1,646 men on both ships suffered 424 killed and 1,222 men rescued (after thirty hours in the sun, in waters inhabited by sharks) by the cruiser [HMS _Enterprise_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Enterprise_(D52) "HMS Enterprise (D52)") and the destroyers [HMS _Paladin_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Paladin_(G69) "HMS Paladin (G69)") and [_Panther_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Panther_(G41) "HMS Panther (G41)").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014406-41)

## Aftermath

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Aftermath")]

### Casualties

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Casualties")]

On land, four Naval officers, 35 ratings, twelve [Goanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goa "Goa") and Indian [Lascars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lascar "Lascar") were killed and 37 civilians, inmates of a psychiatric hospital were killed in the bombing. At sea the Navy suffered the loss of 424 men killed in the sinking of _Dorsetshire_ and _Cornwall_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014405%E2%88%92406-42) Japanese fighter pilots claimed 33 fighters and 11 probables; five were claimed by the Val crews from _Shōkaku_ and one by a Val from _Zuikaku_. The real loss was 21 Hurricanes (two repairable) and several Hurricanes damaged. The Japanese fighter pilots claimed eight Swordfish, two probables and one Swordfish damaged, with a real loss of six. On the British side, 258 Squadron claimed four aircraft shot down, one probable and four damaged for a loss of five pilots killed and two wounded, eight Hurricanes shot down and two badly damaged. In 30 Squadron, 14 aircraft were claimed shot down, with six probables and five aircraft damaged.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201442%E2%80%9343-43)

The Fleet Air Arm pilots of 803 NAS and 806 NAS claimed one Japanese aircraft shot down for a loss of three pilots killed and four Fulmars shot down.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201442%E2%80%9343-43) Anti-aircraft gunners claimed five aircraft shot down for a total of 24 Japanese aircraft confirmed shot down, seven probables and a minimum of nine aircraft damaged. Both sides mistakenly over-claimed; the Japanese lost a Zero from _Sōryū_, three from _Hiryū_ were damaged, five Vals from _Zuikaku_ were shot down and six suffered damage, _Shōkaku_ lost one Val shot down and one damaged. The true total was six Vals and seven damaged, one Zero shot down and three damaged and five Kates damaged. A Japanese bomber pilot crashed and was taken prisoner.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014403%E2%80%93404-44)

The **Air raid on Ceylon (5 April 1942)** also known as the **Easter Sunday raid**, was an air attack on [Colombo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombo "Colombo"), [British Ceylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Ceylon "British Ceylon") (now Sri Lanka) by [Imperial Japanese Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Japanese_Navy "Imperial Japanese Navy") aircraft from the [aircraft carriers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier "Aircraft carrier") of the [1st Air Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Air_Fleet "1st Air Fleet") (_Kidō Butai_) during the Indian Ocean raid (31 March – 10 April 1942). The Japanese plan was to destroy the British [Eastern Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Fleet "Eastern Fleet") in harbour.

The British received warning of the raid in March through decoded Japanese wireless messages and from [air reconnaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_reconnaissance "Air reconnaissance"). The British forestalled the Japanese by dispersing shipping from the harbours in Ceylon before the attack. The Japanese aircraft were met by fighters of [222 Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._222_Group_RAF "No. 222 Group RAF"), [Royal Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Air_Force "Royal Air Force"), the [Fleet Air Arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_Air_Arm "Fleet Air Arm") (FAA) of the [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy") and [anti-aircraft guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_guns "Anti-aircraft guns").

Port facilities were damaged and ships in Colombo harbour were sunk or damaged. The bulk of the Eastern Fleet was not found and survived but several ships were sunk at sea after the raid. The Eastern Fleet moved temporarily to [East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa "East Africa"), from where it sent carrier forces into the central and eastern Indian Ocean. The Japanese Navy was unable to repeat the raid because of its commitments in the Pacific.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

### British Ceylon (Sri Lanka)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: British Ceylon (Sri Lanka)")]

Main article: [British Ceylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Ceylon "British Ceylon")

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Colombo_Map_1930.jpg/250px-Colombo_Map_1930.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colombo_Map_1930.jpg)

1930 diagram of Colombo and the harbour

Ceylon (now [Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka "Sri Lanka")) is off the south-east of India between shipping routes from [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore") and [Rangoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangoon "Rangoon") to the [Red Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea "Red Sea") and the [Persian Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf"). There are natural harbours at Colombo on the south-western coast and Trincomalee on the north-eastern coast, a naval anchorage and base.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014384-2) Ceylon was a geographically important part of the British Empire and its system of trade, communication and military organisation. In the 1930s more shipping tonnage was handled in Ceylon than all the ports of India. Since the beginning of the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), the colonial government had engaged in mass recruitment for local defence, overseas labouring and expanded food production.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJackson2006308-3) Tea and rubber production was emphasised and rubber output rose from 99,500 long tons (101,100 t) in 1941 to 105,500 long tons (107,200 t) in 1943.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurstfield1953168-4) The 3,600 workers in civil engineering converted to the repair and refitting of ships and the manufacture of dummy aircraft, guns and radar installations.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJackson2006308-3)

When the [Pacific War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_War "Pacific War") began on 7 December 1941, the Allied disasters in the Pacific, Malaya and the British débâcle at the [Battle of Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Singapore "Battle of Singapore") in February 1942 made [Colombo Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombo_Harbour "Colombo Harbour") the basis for eastern trade and the centre for the assembly of Indian Ocean convoys. Colombo port was large enough for 45 ships but soon had 100 to 110 ships at once, causing much overcrowding.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMOD1995122-5) The strategic importance of Ceylon increased and British planners deemed the island essential to the defence of [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") and Allied lines of communication through the Indian Ocean. The Allied defeat in the [Dutch East Indies campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_East_Indies_campaign "Dutch East Indies campaign") (11 January – 9 March 1942) left the Indian Ocean vulnerable to Japanese attacks.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBoyd2017364%E2%80%93359-6) The [Malacca Strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malacca_Strait "Malacca Strait") in the Netherlands East Indies was about 1,000 nmi (1,900 km; 1,200 mi) east of Trincomalee, making it a useful base for attacks on Japanese ships sailing to Rangoon in Burma.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014384-2)

From September to December 1941, 710 troop reinforcements arrived on the island and from January to March 1942, another 2,612 arrived; during April and June, 2,112 more troops joined the garrison (2,872) and 4,993 troops moved between the Far East and Ceylon from October 1941 to March 1942.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBehrens1955245,_278-7) The extent of the disasters that befell the British in early 1942, led in March to Admiral Sir [Geoffrey Layton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Layton "Geoffrey Layton") being transferred from the temporary command of the [Eastern Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Fleet "Eastern Fleet") and installed as the Commander-in-Chief, Ceylon, after Admiral [James Somerville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Somerville "James Somerville") arrived to command the fleet. Layton was given authority over the military forces on the island and the civilian authorities of the governor, Sir [Andrew Caldecott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Caldecott "Andrew Caldecott"), "Do not ask permission to do things. Do them and report afterwards what you have done".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJackson2006314,_310-8) Layton found the same complacency and inertia in Ceylon as he had experienced in Malaya,

> ...he takes complete charge of Ceylon and stands no nonsense from anyone.... He pulls all the Ministers legs... and they work for him all the harder.

—Admiral Somerville[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoskill195623%E2%88%9224-9)

### Air defence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Air defence")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Fairey_Fulmar_Mk_I_%28M4062%29.jpg/250px-Fairey_Fulmar_Mk_I_%28M4062%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fairey_Fulmar_Mk_I_(M4062).jpg)

Example of a Fairey Fulmar Mk II

In September 1941 the [Royal Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Air_Force "Royal Air Force") (RAF) had established [No. 222 Group RAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._222_Group_RAF "No. 222 Group RAF") (Air Vice-Marshal [John D'Albiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_D'Albiac "John D'Albiac")) on the island in command of [273 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._273_Squadron_RAF "No. 273 Squadron RAF") at [China Bay airfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Bay_Airport "China Bay Airport") with four [Vickers Vildebeest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vickers_Vildebeest "Vickers Vildebeest") and four [Fairey Seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairey_Seal "Fairey Seal")[torpedo bombers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torpedo_bomber "Torpedo bomber").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJackson2006314,_310-8) Until February 1942, the air defence of Ceylon had been a Royal Navy responsibility and [803 Naval Air Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/803_Naval_Air_Squadron "803 Naval Air Squadron") (803 NAS) and [806 Naval Air Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/806_Naval_Air_Squadron "806 Naval Air Squadron") (806 NAS) had transferred to Ceylon from the Middle East, six [Fairey Fulmars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairey_Fulmar "Fairey Fulmar") at a time. Eight Hurricanes that had been assembled at Karachi, were flown to Ceylon, six of the Hurricanes, ferried to Ceylon by pilots of [136 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._136_Squadron_RAF "No. 136 Squadron RAF"), arrived at [RAF Ratmalana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAF_Ratmalana "RAF Ratmalana") on 23 February. The Torpedo Bomber Reconnaissance Pool, [788 Naval Air Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/788_Naval_Air_Squadron "788 Naval Air Squadron") (788 NAS) with six [Fairey Swordfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairey_Swordfish "Fairey Swordfish") for the Eastern Fleet, was formed on 18 January at China Bay, near [Trincomalee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trincomalee "Trincomalee") and was pressed into service in defence of Ceylon.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWragg2001136ShoresCullIzawa2014384-10)

By March 1942, there were airfields at China Bay near Trincomalee, Ratmalana near Colombo, an airstrip was built at the [Colombo Racecourse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombo_Racecourse "Colombo Racecourse") to relieve congestion at Ratmalana and another airstrip had been built at [Minneriya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minneriya "Minneriya") on the south coast. China Bay was a grass landing ground that had the sea at both ends and there was a ridge along the southern edge; a low ridge ran along the northern boundary. Aircraft could only land and take off to the north-east or south-west, depending on the wind direction. There were fuel storage tanks beyond the north-east corner of the airfield at the Royal Naval Base Trincomalee.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShoresCullIzawa2014384-2) Anti-aircraft defence comprised four obsolescent [QF 3-inch 20 cwt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QF_3-inch_20_cwt "QF 3-inch 20 cwt")[anti-aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft "Anti-aircraft") guns at Trincomalee. The danger of an air attack by aircraft of the Japanese Navy aircraft carriers was acute after the examples of the [Attack on Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor "Attack on Pearl Harbor") in December 1941 and the [Bombing of Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombing_of_Darwin "Bombing of Darwin") in February 1942.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201433-1) The airfields at Ratmalana, near Colombo and China Bay had been expanded.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTERichardsSaunders197570-11)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-13)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/RIHB_2022_PBY_Catalina.jpg/250px-RIHB_2022_PBY_Catalina.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RIHB_2022_PBY_Catalina.jpg)

Example of a Catalina flying boat

On 6 and 7 March the aircraft carrier [HMS _Indomitable_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Indomitable_(92) "HMS Indomitable (92)") dispatched sixty Hurricanes of [30 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._30_Squadron_RAF "No. 30 Squadron RAF") and [261 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._261_Squadron_RAF "No. 261 Squadron RAF"), that had been intended for Java. On 30 March, the RAF reconstituted [258 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._258_Squadron_RAF "No. 258 Squadron RAF") that had been mauled in the fighting in [British Malaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Malaya "British Malaya"), [Sumatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumatra "Sumatra") and [Java](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java "Java").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJackson2006314-14) By 4 April, 803 NAS and 806 NAS of the [Fleet Air Arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_Air_Arm "Fleet Air Arm") were ready with 24 Fulmars; the ground defences had been reinforced to 144 anti-aircraft guns. On 5 April, there were 37–38 serviceable Hurricanes near Colombo.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201444,_42,_35-15)

The first [Consolidated PBY Catalina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consolidated_PBY_Catalina "Consolidated PBY Catalina") long-range flying boat of [413 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/413_Squadron "413 Squadron")[Royal Canadian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Canadian_Air_Force "Royal Canadian Air Force") (RCAF) arrived on 28 March, with the ground crews following on by sea, two more arrived before the raid and on 6 and 7 April two more Canadian Catalinas arrived.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGreenhous1994386-16) By 4 April, four [205 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._205_Squadron_RAF "No. 205 Squadron RAF") RAF Catalinas had reached the island. There was one operational Dutch Catalina of the [Netherlands Naval Aviation Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_Naval_Aviation_Service "Netherlands Naval Aviation Service") (MLD); two of the RAF and three Dutch Catalinas were unserviceable. The Catalinas were based at [Koggala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koggala_Airport "Koggala Airport")[lagoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koggala_Lagoon "Koggala Lagoon"), at the south end of the island.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201433,_35,_44,_37-12)

### Radar

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_raid_on_Ceylon_(5_April_1942)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Radar")]

Main article: [Air Ministry Experimental Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Ministry_Experimental_Station "Air Ministry Experimental Station")

Radar stations, code-named Air Ministry Experimental Stations (AMES) were established at the [Royal Colombo Golf Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Colombo_Golf_Club "Royal Colombo Golf Club") at Ridgeway about 6 mi (9.7 km) north of Ratmalana airfield (AMES 254) and at Trincomalee (AMES 272). AMES 254 personnel arrived on 18 March and the equipment four days later. AMES 254 became operational on 25 March and was linked by telephone to 20 Operations Room on 28 March. The terrain around the radar limited maximum range to 60 mi (97 km) and the altitude of an object affected the detection range. The short notice may not have been sufficient for operators to tell the difference between false radar echoes produced by local conditions and real ones. The aerial projected "[lobes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiation_pattern "Radiation pattern")" in which objects might be detected, with gaps between some lobes or lobes overlapping. The distance travelled by an aircraft between the maximum range of AMES 254 to Ratmalana was 54 mi (87 km) A Zero took about 17 minutes to cover the distance and it took a Hurricane five minutes to take off and six more to climb to interception altitude. There were only six minutes for AMES 254 to report to 20 Operations Room and for orders to be issued if pilots were going to avoid being caught climbing.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday_Raid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStuart201439%E2%80%9341-17)
